# Angular Philosophies (full text)

Source: https://github.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies. Every chapter follows, in order. Code in templates/ is linked from the chapters.

---

# Philosophy

This is how I write Angular apps, written down so a team, a new hire or an AI agent can write them the same way. It
targets Angular 22 with TypeScript 6.0, zoneless, signals everywhere, NgRx SignalStore for state, and an Nx workspace
split by business domain.

It is a set of defaults, not a law. Every rule comes with the reason behind it, so you can tell when your situation is
different enough to break one.

## Code is a necessary evil

Every line you write is a line someone reads, tests, upgrades and eventually deletes. The best change is the one you
didn't have to make, and the second best is the smallest one that works.

- **Build what is needed today.** YAGNI is the most useful rule I know. A flag, a config option or an abstraction for
  a case that might come later usually costs more than adding it later, because later you know what the case really is.
- **Don't be clever.** Clever code is read at 3am by someone who didn't write it. Boring and obvious wins.
- **Think before adding a dependency.** If the platform does it, use the platform. Angular 22 already ships
  `httpResource`, signal inputs, `linkedSignal`, a router, forms and a control flow syntax. Reach for a library when
  the problem is real, not when the tutorial used one.
- **Delete before you add.** Removing unused code, an old wrapper or a flag nobody sets is progress.
- **Write an abstraction the third time, not the first.** Two copies are cheaper than the wrong shared function. This
  is also how the custom store features in [06-custom-features.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/06-custom-features.md) are meant to appear.

## Leave it better than you found it

When you touch a file, fix the small smell next to your change or leave a `TODO` with a reason. Don't start a rewrite
inside a feature branch. Refactor in small steps with the tests green, and make the next person's change easier than yours
was.

## One place for each thing

Most arguments about structure go away when each kind of code has exactly one home:

- Server state, API calls and the facade a page talks to live in a **signal store**.
- A page's markup and its wiring live in a **component**.
- Anything two features need lives in a **library** with a tag that says what it may depend on.
- A rule a machine can check is a **lint rule**, not a paragraph in a wiki.

[01-architecture.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/01-architecture.md) and [03-signal-store.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/03-signal-store.md) are these ideas made specific.

## Make the right thing the easy thing

Conventions only survive if following them is less work than ignoring them. That is why this repo ships templates (a
store, a test toolkit, config files) and AI instructions as well as prose. Copy the template, change the names, and you
are already following the guide.

## Accessibility and Arabic are not extras

A page that can't be used with a keyboard, or can't be read at arm's length, is not finished. A layout that breaks in
right-to-left is not finished either. Both are cheap to do from the first commit and expensive to retrofit, so they are
part of the defaults. See [07-forms-routing-i18n.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/07-forms-routing-i18n.md) and [08-accessibility.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/08-accessibility.md).

## How to read the rest

Each chapter ends with a short list of rules. The text explains the why; the rules are what a linter, a reviewer or
an AI agent checks. If a rule and the text disagree, the rule is the bug, so open an issue.

| Chapter | What it settles |
| --- | --- |
| [01 Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/01-architecture.md) | How the workspace is divided and what may import what |
| [02 Components](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/02-components.md) | How a component, a template and a file are written |
| [03 Signal store](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/03-signal-store.md) | The shape of every store and who provides it |
| [04 Data access](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/04-data-access.md) | Reading, writing, errors and interceptors |
| [05 Toolkit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/05-toolkit.md) | Which `@ngrx-toolkit/core` features to use and which to leave |
| [06 Custom features](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/06-custom-features.md) | Writing your own `signalStoreFeature` |
| [07 Forms, routing, i18n](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/07-forms-routing-i18n.md) | Forms, lazy routes, translations, RTL |
| [08 Accessibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/08-accessibility.md) | Contrast, focus, keyboard, meaning without colour |
| [09 Testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/09-testing.md) | How to write a spec, with a toolkit to copy |
| [10 Tooling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/10-tooling.md) | pnpm, Nx, ESLint, Prettier, commits |
| [11 Using with AI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/11-using-with-ai.md) | Skill, plugin, `llms.txt`, `AGENTS.md`, Cursor rules, MCP |

## Rules

<!-- rules -->
- Build only what the current task needs; do not add flags, options or abstractions for hypothetical cases.
- Prefer the Angular platform (`httpResource`, signal APIs, router, forms) over a new dependency.
- Write a shared abstraction the third time the same code appears, not the first.
- When touching a file, fix nearby smells or leave a `TODO` with a reason; never rewrite inside a feature branch.
- Express every rule a machine can check as a lint rule or a type, not as documentation.
- Treat accessibility and right-to-left support as part of "done", not as follow-up work.
<!-- /rules -->

# Architecture

A large Angular app stays maintainable when it is cut into domains and layers that a tool, not a person, keeps in
order. The examples use a small shop with two business domains, `orders` and `billing`, plus `shared` code.

## The workspace

```
apps/
  storefront/                  the Angular app: routes, providers, one folder per feature
libs/
  orders/                      scope:orders
    data-access/               stores and API services          type:data-access
    feature/checkout/          a full page with its own store   type:feature
    ui/                        presentational components        type:ui
    util/                      pure functions                   type:util
  billing/                     scope:billing, same layout
  shared/                      scope:shared: nothing business-specific lives here
    ui/  util/  core/  testing/
```

Libraries are split by **type** inside a **domain**. A new business concept gets a domain folder; it does not get a new
top-level layout.

## Tags: two per library

Every library has exactly one `scope` tag (who owns it) and one `type` tag (what kind of code it is), set in its
`project.json`:

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `scope:orders`, `scope:billing` | Belongs to that business domain |
| `scope:shared` | Generic, usable by any domain, never imports a domain |
| `scope:app` | An application, which may use every scope |
| `type:util` | Pure functions. No Angular injection, no services |
| `type:data-access` | Signal stores and HTTP services |
| `type:core` | Angular infrastructure: providers, interceptors, guards, models |
| `type:ui` | Presentational components: inputs and outputs only |
| `type:feature` | Smart components: a routed page with its own store |
| `type:shell` | The layout that mounts features, used only by an app |
| `type:testing` | Test helpers, imported by specs only |

## Dependencies flow down

A library may import only from the layers below it. `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` turns that into a build error, so
nobody has to remember it.

```
type:shell        mounts features, used only by an app
type:feature      pages
type:ui           presentational components
type:core         providers, interceptors, guards, models
type:data-access  stores, API services
type:util         pure functions
```

Scope follows the same logic: a domain may import itself and `shared`, `shared` imports only `shared`, and a domain
never imports another domain. If `billing` needs something from `orders`, it is either shared code in the wrong place or
a sign the two should talk through an event (see [06-custom-features.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/06-custom-features.md)). The complete lint
configuration is in [templates/config/eslint.boundaries.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/config/eslint.boundaries.js).

Two details come from running this in production:

- `type:data-access` may import `type:core`, because stores need the HTTP configuration and error types. The reverse is
  forbidden: core never imports a store.
- `util` libraries accept what they need as parameters. A date helper takes the language as an argument instead of
  injecting a language service, which keeps it testable without Angular.

## Where does new code go

| You are adding | Put it in |
| --- | --- |
| A store or API service for a domain | `libs/<domain>/data-access` |
| A page with its own store | `libs/<domain>/feature/<name>` |
| A component two features reuse | `libs/<domain>/ui`, or `libs/shared/ui` if it knows no domain |
| A type shared across libs | `libs/shared/core` (models) |
| An HTTP interceptor | `libs/shared/core`, in an `interceptors` entry point |
| A route guard | `libs/shared/core` for generic ones, the domain's `data-access` for domain ones |
| A pure date, string or number helper | `libs/shared/util` |
| A test helper | `libs/shared/testing` |
| Code used by one feature only | **Inside that feature.** Do not create a library yet |

The last row matters most. **Code stays in the app until a second consumer appears, then it is promoted to a
library.** Promoting early produces libraries with one user and a public API nobody needed.

## Entry points and public APIs

Split a library with Angular secondary entry points when it holds distinct parts (`@shop/shared/core/models`,
`@shop/shared/core/interceptors`), not with more libraries. Each entry has its own `index.ts`, and:

- Export by name. Do not `export *` runtime code, only types, so the public surface stays deliberate.
- Import through the path alias (`@shop/orders/data-access`), never through a relative `../../` path.
- Inside the app, `@/*` points at `src/app/*`, so a feature imports its neighbours the same way.

Nx boundaries only apply between projects, not between entry points inside one project. When two entries of one library
must never import each other, add a `no-restricted-imports` rule to that library's own ESLint config. A guest checkout
and a signed-in checkout inside one `checkout` library are the typical case: they share a domain and must not share
code that depends on a session.

When both sides need the same piece, choose in this order:

1. **Reuse** what does not depend on the session or the domain: `shared/ui`, `shared/util`.
2. **Promote, then reuse** when it can work through inputs and outputs only, with no store and no session.
3. **Duplicate** when sharing it would need an `if (guest)` flag. Two small copies that can change independently are
   cheaper than one function with a mode switch.

## Naming

| Thing | Convention | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nx project | `<scope>-<type>-<name>` | `orders-data-access` |
| Path alias | `@<workspace>/<scope>/<type>` | `@shop/orders/data-access` |
| Component file | `<name>.component.ts` + `.component.html` | `order-list.component.ts` |
| Store, service, model | `<name>.store.ts`, `.service.ts`, `.model.ts` | `order-list.store.ts` |
| Routes, guard | `<feature>.routes.ts`, `<name>.guard.ts` | `checkout.routes.ts` |
| Spec | beside its source, `<file>.spec.ts` | `order-list.store.spec.ts` |
| Selector | `app-` prefix, kebab-case | `app-order-list` |

## Rules

<!-- rules -->
- Give every library exactly one `scope:*` tag and one `type:*` tag in its `project.json`.
- Enforce module boundaries with `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries`; dependencies flow only downward through util, data-access, core, ui, feature, shell.
- Never let a domain import another domain, and never let `scope:shared` import a domain.
- Keep code inside the app feature until a second consumer exists; then promote it to a library.
- Split a library with secondary entry points, not with extra libraries.
- Export by name from each `index.ts`; do not `export *` runtime code.
- Import through path aliases (`@shop/...`, `@/...`); never use `../../` across feature or library boundaries.
- Make `type:util` code free of Angular injection; pass language and configuration as parameters.
- Forbid sibling entry points from importing each other with `no-restricted-imports` in the library's own ESLint config.
- Duplicate small code instead of adding an `if (guest)`-style mode flag to a shared function.
- Name files `<name>.component.ts`, `<name>.store.ts`, `<name>.service.ts`, `<name>.model.ts`, `<feature>.routes.ts`, and keep each spec beside its source.
<!-- /rules -->

---

# Components

Angular 22 removed most of the ceremony. A component is a class with a template, and the defaults are the ones you want:
standalone, `OnPush`, and no zone. Write the least that works.

## What a component looks like

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-order-list',
  templateUrl: './order-list.component.html',
  providers: [OrderListStore],
  host: { class: 'block p-4' },
})
export class OrderListComponent {
  protected readonly store = inject(OrderListStore);
  protected readonly statuses = ORDER_STATUS_OPTIONS;
}
```

The full file and its template are in [templates/signal-store/](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/order-list.component.ts). Notice
what is missing:

- **No `standalone: true`.** It is the default.
- **No `changeDetection: OnPush`.** In Angular 22 `OnPush` is the default (`ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager` is the opt-out).
  Don't edit old files only to remove it, but don't add it to new ones.
- **No constructor.** Dependencies come from `inject()` in field initialisers.
- **No `@HostBinding` or `@HostListener`.** Use the `host: {}` object.
- **No `NgModule`, no `CommonModule`, no `ngClass`, no `ngStyle`.** Bind `[class.active]` and `[style.width.px]`.
- **No `ngOnInit` for loading data.** Reads are resources derived from state, see [04-data-access.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/04-data-access.md).

## Zoneless

Apps run with `provideZonelessChangeDetection()` and no `zone.js`. Change detection runs when a signal read by a
template changes, an event handler runs, or `markForCheck` is called. In practice that means one rule: **state a template
reads must be a signal.** A plain field that you mutate will not update the screen.

## Signals, all the way

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| An input | `input()` or `input.required<T>()` |
| Two-way binding | `model()` |
| An output | `output<T>()` |
| A query | `viewChild()`, `contentChildren()` |
| Local state | `signal()` |
| Derived state | `computed()` |
| State that follows another signal but stays writable | `linkedSignal()` |
| Shared or page state | a signal store, see [03-signal-store.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/03-signal-store.md) |

Keep `effect()` for side effects that leave Angular (writing to `localStorage`, calling a third-party widget). If you are
using an effect to set a signal from another signal, you wanted `computed` or `linkedSignal`.

## Templates

- Use `@if`, `@for` and `@switch`. `@for` always has a `track`, and `track item.id` beats `track $index` when items have ids.
- Use `@empty` for the empty list, and `@defer` for heavy parts below the fold.
- No logic in templates beyond a condition or a call to a signal. Put the rest in a `computed`.
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for static images.
- Put a `data-testid` on interactive elements and on the elements tests assert on. See [09-testing.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/09-testing.md).
- Use `@let` for a value you read three times in one template.

## Pages and presentational components

Two kinds of component, kept apart:

- **Page (smart).** Routed or a feature root. Provides its store, injects it, passes data down. Lives in a `type:feature` library.
- **Presentational (dumb).** Inputs and outputs only. It never injects a store or `HttpClient`, so it can be reused and tested
  with `render(Component, [], { inputs })`. Lives in a `type:ui` library.

A component that needs both is a page that contains a presentational component. Split it.

## Files and naming

- `order-list.component.ts`, `order-list.component.html`, `order-list.component.spec.ts`, side by side.
- The class is `OrderListComponent`, matching the file name. Selectors use the `app-` prefix.
- The template lives in its own `.html` file. Inline a template only when it is a few lines and has no logic.
- Styling uses utility classes and design tokens. No per-component stylesheets, no hex colours, no arbitrary pixel values.
- Named exports. A routed component is loaded with `loadComponent: () => import('./order-list.component').then(m => m.OrderListComponent)`.

## Services

A service that holds no state and does one job is a plain `@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })` class. Anything with state
that a page shares is a store, not a service. Angular 22 also ships a `@Service()` decorator; this guide keeps
`@Injectable` for now because every tool and library in the ecosystem understands it.

## Rules

<!-- rules -->
- Write components as standalone without `standalone: true`, and without `changeDetection` (OnPush is the Angular 22 default).
- Inject dependencies with `inject()` in field initialisers; do not use constructors for injection.
- Use the `host: {}` object; never `@HostBinding` or `@HostListener`.
- Use `input()`, `model()`, `output()`, `viewChild()`; do not use the decorator forms in new code.
- Run zoneless with `provideZonelessChangeDetection()`; every value a template reads must be a signal.
- Use `computed` or `linkedSignal` to derive state; use `effect()` only for side effects outside Angular.
- Use `@if`, `@for` (always with `track`), `@switch`, `@empty`, `@defer`; never `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `ngClass` or `ngStyle`.
- Keep templates free of logic beyond a condition; move the rest into a `computed`.
- Keep presentational components free of stores and `HttpClient`; they take inputs and emit outputs.
- Put pages in `type:feature` libraries and presentational components in `type:ui` libraries.
- Add `data-testid` to interactive elements and to elements that tests assert on.
- Use named exports and `loadComponent` with a `.then(m => m.XComponent)` for routed components.
- Use utility classes and design tokens for styling; no hex colours and no per-component stylesheets.
- Keep `@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })` for stateless services; put shared state in a signal store.
<!-- /rules -->

---

# The signal store

NgRx SignalStore is the centre of this guide. It gives a page one object with its state, its derived values, its API calls
and its actions, built from small features that compose. Everything here targets `@ngrx/signals` 22.

## The rule

**A `signalStore` is the facade, the API layer and the state layer for its slice.** It is not a plain service next to a
store next to some `.subscribe()` wiring. From that follow three consequences:

- Components inject a store and read signals. They never inject `HttpClient` or a data service.
- Components never `.subscribe()`. Anything reactive is a signal, a resource or an `rxMethod`.
- Components never call a `load()` method after a filter changes. Reads are resources derived from state, so changing the
  filter signal changes the request. See [04-data-access.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/04-data-access.md).

## One store per view

When a feature has a list, a detail page and a form, each page gets its own store:

```
orders/
  order.model.ts          types and static option lists. No store, no injection
  order.store.ts          feature store: reference data every view needs, providedIn: 'root'
  order-list/
    order-list.store.ts   view store, provided by the component
    order-list.component.ts
    order-list.component.html
  order-form/
    order-form.store.ts   view store, provided by the component
    ...
```

Do not merge list state and form state because they belong to the same feature. Each view owns its filters, paging, dialog
state and its own reads and writes.

| Store | Provided | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Feature store (reference data, lookups) | `{ providedIn: 'root' }` | Stable for the session and shared by every view, so it is fetched once |
| View store (list, detail, form) | `providers: [OrderListStore]` on the component | Filters, paging and dialog state must reset when the user leaves, not leak into the next visit |
| Cross-feature state (auth, layout) | a library store, `providedIn: 'root'` | Owned by a library, never by one feature |

State shared by two features belongs in a library store. A feature must never reach into another feature's store.

## The shape of a store

The full file is [templates/signal-store/order-list.store.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/order-list.store.ts). The skeleton:

```ts
interface OrderListState {
  page: number;
  search: string;
  status: OrderStatus | null;
}

const initialState: OrderListState = { page: 1, search: '', status: null };

export const OrderListStore = signalStore(
  guardedDevtools('orderList'),
  withState(initialState),
  withProps(...),       // injected services, debounced signals, private helpers
  withResource(...),    // reads
  withMutations(...),   // writes
  withComputed(...),    // derived values
  withMethods(...),     // actions
);
```

The order is deliberate. Each feature can use what the ones above it added, so state comes first and methods last.

- **Type the state** with an interface and name the starting value `initialState`. A store that outlives its page also
  exposes `reset()`, which is `patchState(store, initialState)`.
- **Change state only with `patchState`.** Never mutate an array or an object in place; replace it.
- **Put derived values in `withComputed`**, not in methods and not in the template.
- **Inject with `inject()` inside `withProps`, `withMethods` or `withHooks`.** A store has no constructor.
- **Prefix private members with `_`.** Underscore-prefixed state, props and methods are not exposed on the store instance, so
  `_debouncedSearch` and `_listReload` stay inside the store. Expose a deliberate method (`refresh()`) when callers need it.
- **Reset the page when a filter changes.** Every filter setter patches `page: 1` in the same call, because a filter applied
  on page 5 can leave you past the last page.
- **Never type a store as `any`.** If declaration emit complains in a library, export an interface for the public surface.

## Commands that are not plain requests

A search that must not overlap itself, or a command with several steps, is better as an `rxMethod`:

```ts
search: rxMethod<string>(
  pipe(
    tap(() => store.setLoading()),
    exhaustMap(q =>
      http.get<Page<Product>>('/api/products', { params: { q } }).pipe(
        tapResponse({
          next: ({ items }) => patchState(store, { products: items }),
          error: () => store.setError('search-failed'),
        }),
      ),
    ),
  ),
),
```

Choose the flattening operator on purpose: `switchMap` for a search where only the latest matters, `exhaustMap` for a submit
that must not run twice, `concatMap` when order matters. The complete store is
[product-search.store.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/product-search.store.ts). It also shows `setLoading` and `setError`,
which come from the custom feature in [06-custom-features.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/06-custom-features.md).

Reach for `rxMethod` when you need operators. A request derived from state is a resource, and a plain command is a mutation.

## State that survives a reload

Persist with `withStorageSync`, never with hand-written `localStorage.getItem` calls. See
[05-toolkit.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/05-toolkit.md) and [layout.store.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/layout.store.ts), which persists only the
theme and the language and leaves `sidebarCollapsed` alone.

## Testing a store

A store spec injects the store with a fake `HttpClient`, drives it through its public methods and asserts on its signals.
The complete example is
[order-list.store.spec.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/testing/examples/order-list.store.spec.ts), and [09-testing.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/09-testing.md)
explains the toolkit it uses. Every store gets a spec.

## Rules

<!-- rules -->
- Make a `signalStore` the facade, API layer and state layer for its slice; components never inject `HttpClient` or a data service.
- Never call `.subscribe()` in a component; use signals, resources or `rxMethod`.
- Never add a `load()` method that a component must call after a filter changes; derive reads from state with resources.
- Use one store per view (list, detail, form), provided by the component with `providers: [XStore]`.
- Provide a feature store for shared reference data with `{ providedIn: 'root' }`; put cross-feature state in a library store.
- Never let a feature import another feature's store.
- Type state with an interface, name the starting value `initialState`, and expose `reset()` when the store outlives its page.
- Change state only with `patchState`; never mutate arrays or objects in place.
- Put derived values in `withComputed`; inject dependencies with `inject()` inside `withProps`, `withMethods` or `withHooks`.
- Prefix private store members with `_` and expose a deliberate method when callers need them.
- Reset `page` to 1 in every filter setter.
- Never type a store as `any`.
- Use `rxMethod` only when operators are needed; choose `switchMap`, `exhaustMap` or `concatMap` deliberately.
- Persist state with `withStorageSync`, never with hand-written `localStorage` calls.
- Give every store a spec.
<!-- /rules -->

---

# Data access

How a page reads from the server, writes to it, and shows what went wrong. The tools are `httpResource` for reads,
`httpMutation` for writes, functional interceptors for everything cross-cutting, and signals for the result.

## Reads: resources derived from state

A read is a resource whose request is computed from signals. When a signal the request reads changes, the resource
refetches by itself. Nobody calls `load()`.

```ts
withResource(
  store => ({
    list: httpResource<Page<Order>>(
      () => ({ url: '/api/orders', params: { page: store.page(), ...(store.status() ? { status: store.status()! } : {}) } }),
      { defaultValue: EMPTY_PAGE },
    ),
  }),
  { errorHandling: 'previous value' },
),
```

`withResource` comes from `@ngrx-toolkit/core` and is marked `@experimental` in v22. A named resource adds
`listValue()`, `listStatus()`, `listError()`, `listIsLoading()` and a private `_listReload()` to the store. A component
reads those signals and nothing else.

Two things go on every resource, and neither is optional:

- **A `defaultValue`.** Without one the value type is `T | undefined`, and every consumer needs a `?.` or a `??`.
- **`errorHandling: 'previous value'`.** The default (`'undefined value'`) widens the type the same way.

Together they keep the value non-nullable end to end, so `store.listValue().items` is always an array. If you find
yourself writing `?.` on a resource value in a component, the store is missing one of the two. Fix the store.

### What "previous value" does and does not keep

This is worth knowing exactly, because it is easy to assume more than it does.

| Situation | What `listValue()` holds |
| --- | --- |
| A reload of the same request fails (`refresh()`) | The last good value. `listError()` is set, so the page can say the data is stale |
| A changed filter or page starts a new request and it fails | The `defaultValue`. A new request is not a reload, so there is no previous value to keep |

Both are covered by tests in [order-list.store.spec.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/testing/examples/order-list.store.spec.ts). Design the
page for both: show the stale list with a "try again" button after a failed reload, and show the empty state plus an error
after a failed filter.

### A read that only one component needs

A resource used by one component and nothing else can live in the component with plain `httpResource`. Move it into a store
when a second component needs the result or the call becomes a command. A page reading several resources folds their
statuses into one with [`apiStatus`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/api-status.ts), so the template has a single skeleton and a
single error state:

```ts
protected readonly status = apiStatus(this.orders.status, this.stats.status);
```

## Writes: mutations, not resources

`httpResource` is for GET. Every POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE is an `httpMutation`:

```ts
withMutations(store => ({
  cancel: httpMutation({
    request: (id: number) => ({ url: `/api/orders/${id}/cancel`, method: 'POST', body: {} }),
    onSuccess: () => store._listReload(),
  }),
})),
```

Each mutation exposes `cancelIsPending()`, `cancelStatus()`, `cancelError()`, and the method itself returns a promise of a
result, so a component can `await store.cancel(id)` and branch on the status. Check the API's real verbs first: if it has
no `PUT`, a save is `PATCH` when an id exists and `POST` when it doesn't, and one mutation can pick between them in its
`request` function.

A successful write reloads the reads it affected, inside `onSuccess`, so the list and the stats never disagree.

## Don't fetch what you already know

If an endpoint returns a compile-time constant (the values of an enum, a fixed list of options), do not call it. Put the
constant in the model file (`ORDER_STATUS_OPTIONS`) and use it. The endpoint can keep existing for other consumers; stopping
one call is not a reason to delete a route. Search the whole repository for other callers before removing either side.

## Interceptors

Cross-cutting HTTP behaviour lives in functional interceptors, registered once, in order, by a single provider function
such as `provideShopInterceptors()`:

| Interceptor | Job |
| --- | --- |
| API prefix | Adds the base URL from configuration |
| Clean query params | Drops empty and `undefined` params so a store doesn't have to |
| Accept-Language | Sends the current language, so a language change refetches in the right one |
| Response unwrap | Unwraps a `{ data }` envelope if the backend uses one |
| Error | Turns a failed request into a typed error and a toast |
| Unauthorised | Sends a 401 to the login page and clears the session |

Anything that needs an exception, such as a guest flow that must not send credentials, asks for it with an `HttpContext`
token (`GUEST_REQUEST`) that the interceptor reads. The interceptor never matches feature URLs, because then the core
library would know about its features.

## Errors

- Backend errors are typed once (`ApiError`, `ApiErrorResult` in the core models) and mapped by the error interceptor.
- A failed read shows an error state with a retry that calls the store's `refresh()`. A failed write shows a toast or an
  inline message, chosen by where the user is looking.
- Translate the message. Interceptors and stores carry translation keys, and the template translates them.
- Track `status` and `error` in state for commands built with `rxMethod`; resources and mutations track their own.

## Rules

<!-- rules -->
- Read server data with resources derived from state (`httpResource` via `withResource`); never with a `load()` method.
- Give every resource a `defaultValue` and `{ errorHandling: 'previous value' }`; never write `?.` or `??` on a resource value in a component.
- Design pages for both failure cases: a failed reload keeps the last value, a failed changed request falls back to the `defaultValue`.
- Keep a resource in its component only while one component uses it; move it into a store when a second needs it.
- Fold several resource statuses into one with `apiStatus` so a page has one loading state and one error state.
- Write with `withMutations` and `httpMutation`; never use `httpResource` for POST, PATCH, PUT or DELETE.
- Reload the affected reads in a mutation's `onSuccess`.
- Check the API's real verbs before choosing PUT or PATCH.
- Never call an endpoint for a compile-time constant; keep it as a `const` in the model file.
- Search the whole repository for other callers before deleting a frontend call or a backend route.
- Implement cross-cutting HTTP behaviour as functional interceptors registered by one provider function.
- Never let an interceptor match feature URLs; use an `HttpContext` token for exceptions.
- Type backend errors once and show failures through translation keys.
<!-- /rules -->

---

# The toolkit

`@ngrx-toolkit/core` adds extensions on top of `@ngrx/signals`: resources, mutations, devtools, storage sync and more. It
ships more than most features need, and every extension is a thing a reader has to learn. This chapter says what is
adopted, what is available but not yet needed, and what to avoid.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @ngrx/signals @ngrx-toolkit/core
```

Starting with version 22 the package is **`@ngrx-toolkit/core`**. Version 21 and earlier were published as
`@angular-architects/ngrx-toolkit`. Match its major to your Angular major; v22 needs `@angular/core` 22, `@ngrx/signals` 22
and `@ngrx/store` 22 as peers.

## Inventory

**Adopted.** These are part of the standard store:

| Extension | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `withResource` | Reads, derived from state. See [04-data-access.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/04-data-access.md) |
| `withMutations`, `httpMutation` | Writes. `rxMutation` for a write that is not a plain HTTP call |
| `withDevtools`, `withDevToolsStub` | Only through `guardedDevtools`, below |
| `withMapper` | Redacting sensitive keys before they reach devtools |
| `withStorageSync` | Persisting part of a store to `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` |

**Available, add when a real need shows up.** Don't add these speculatively:

| Extension | Add it when |
| --- | --- |
| `withImmutableState` | A store mutated outside `patchState` caused a real bug. It throws in dev mode on such a mutation |
| `withReset` | A store needs a `resetState()` and the hand-written `reset()` has become repetitive |
| `withConditional` | You must swap between two feature sets of the same shape by a condition |
| `withUndoRedo` | A screen offers undo and redo |
| `withCallState` | A store is built on `rxMethod` and repeats `loading` and `error` flags. Resources and mutations already track their own status. See [06-custom-features.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/06-custom-features.md) for a smaller version |

**Leave alone.** These solve a shape of problem this guide avoids:

| Extension | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| `withDataService`, `withEntityResources` | Both assume the endpoint returns a bare array. A paginated envelope (`{ items, total }`) doesn't fit; use `withResource` |
| `withPagination` | Client-side paging of a collection that is already loaded. Server-side paging doesn't need it |
| `withRedux`, `createEffects` | A reducer and effects layer that this guide's facade rule exists to avoid. The toolkit's own docs mark `createEffects` deprecated in favour of `@ngrx/signals/events`. See [06-custom-features.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/06-custom-features.md) |
| `withFeatureFactory` | Deprecated. Use `withFeature` from `@ngrx/signals` |
| `patchState` from the toolkit | Deprecated alias of `updateState`. Use `patchState` from `@ngrx/signals` |

If you add an extension that is not marked adopted, update this table in the same change. The inventory is what stops the
toolkit from slowly becoming the whole architecture.

## Devtools, never raw

`withDevtools` connects to the Redux DevTools browser extension unconditionally. It does not check `isDevMode()`. A raw
`withDevtools()` call therefore ships to production, where anyone with the extension installed can read that store's
state. Every store goes through one wrapper:

```ts
import { isDevMode } from '@angular/core';
import { DevtoolsFeature, withDevToolsStub, withDevtools } from '@ngrx-toolkit/core';

export function guardedDevtools(name: string, ...features: DevtoolsFeature[]) {
  return isDevMode() ? withDevtools(name, ...features) : withDevToolsStub(name, ...features);
}
```

`withDevToolsStub` is the toolkit's own mechanism for this: it never touches the devtools connection. Keep one copy of the
wrapper in a shared `util` or `core` library, and grep for `withDevtools(` before merging. It should only appear inside
that file. The file is [guarded-devtools.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/guarded-devtools.ts).

When a store's tracked state holds a full entity row, also pass `withMapper` and redact any password-, token- or
secret-shaped key before it reaches devtools. That is defence in depth on top of the server not sending those fields. A
store that holds only ids, names and counts has nothing to mask, so don't add one.

## Storage sync

```ts
withStorageSync({
  key: 'app-layout',
  select: ({ theme, language }) => ({ theme, language }), // persist only what should survive a reload
}),
```

Place it right after `withState`. By default it reads on init and writes on every state change, so methods that used to
call `localStorage.setItem` after `patchState` simply drop that call. `select` keeps transient state such as
`sidebarCollapsed` out of storage. See [layout.store.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/layout.store.ts).

Guard any direct `window` access for server rendering. Storage sync handles that for you, hand-written code doesn't.

## Rules

<!-- rules -->
- Install `@ngrx-toolkit/core` for Angular 22 (`@angular-architects/ngrx-toolkit` for 21 and earlier), with the same major as Angular.
- Use `withResource`, `withMutations`/`httpMutation`, `guardedDevtools`, `withMapper` and `withStorageSync` as the standard extensions.
- Add `withImmutableState`, `withReset`, `withConditional`, `withUndoRedo` or `withCallState` only when a real need appears, and update the inventory in the same change.
- Do not use `withDataService`, `withEntityResources`, `withPagination`, `withRedux`, `createEffects` or `withFeatureFactory`.
- Use `withFeature` from `@ngrx/signals` instead of `withFeatureFactory`, and `patchState` from `@ngrx/signals` instead of the toolkit's.
- Never call `withDevtools` directly; call `guardedDevtools(name, ...)` from one shared file.
- Add `withMapper` to redact secret-shaped keys when a store's tracked state holds a full entity row.
- Persist state with `withStorageSync` and a `select` that lists only what should survive a reload; place it right after `withState`.
<!-- /rules -->

---

# Custom store features

`signalStoreFeature` lets you package state, computed values and methods as one reusable piece, and put it in any store
with a single line. It is the most powerful thing in SignalStore and the easiest to overuse.

## When to write one

**Write a feature the third time you copy the same block between stores.** Not before.

A feature written on the first use guesses at what varies. After three real copies you know which parts are the same and
which differ, and the feature takes exactly those as parameters. This is the same rule as
[the philosophy chapter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/00-philosophy.md): write the abstraction the third time.

Three blocks that show up again and again in list and search stores, and are the usual first features:

| Feature | The repeated code |
| --- | --- |
| `withRequestStatus()` | A `loading` flag, an `error` flag and a `loaded` flag that can disagree, in every `rxMethod` store |
| `withServerPagination()` | `page`, `pageSize`, `total`, `pageCount` and a `setPage` in every list store |
| `withFilters()` | A filter patch that also has to send the user back to page 1 |

Reads built on resources and writes built on mutations don't need `withRequestStatus`: they already expose `status`,
`isLoading` and `error`. It exists for stores built on `rxMethod`.

## A feature with state, computed values and methods

```ts
export type RequestStatus = 'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error';

export function withRequestStatus() {
  return signalStoreFeature(
    withState<{ status: RequestStatus; error: string | null }>({ status: 'idle', error: null }),
    withComputed(({ status }) => ({
      isLoading: computed(() => status() === 'loading'),
      isSuccess: computed(() => status() === 'success'),
      isError: computed(() => status() === 'error'),
    })),
    withMethods(store => ({
      setLoading() { patchState(store, { status: 'loading', error: null }); },
      setSuccess() { patchState(store, { status: 'success', error: null }); },
      setError(error: string) { patchState(store, { status: 'error', error }); },
    })),
  );
}
```

One `status` field cannot be `loading` and `error` at once, which the three-flag version can. The file is
[with-request-status.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/with-request-status.ts), and
[product-search.store.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/product-search.store.ts) uses it with `rxMethod`.

## A feature that needs another feature

When a feature depends on something the store must already have, say so with `type<>()` in the first argument. The compiler
then rejects the store if the dependency is missing or in the wrong order:

```ts
export function withFilters<F extends Record<string, unknown>>(initial: F) {
  return signalStoreFeature(
    { methods: type<{ firstPage(): void }>() },
    withState({ filters: initial }),
    withMethods(store => ({
      patchFilters(patch: Partial<F>) {
        patchState(store, s => ({ filters: { ...s.filters, ...patch } }));
        store.firstPage();
      },
    })),
  );
}
```

`withFilters` needs `firstPage()`, which `withServerPagination()` provides, so it must come after it in the store. See
[with-filters.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/with-filters.ts) and
[with-server-pagination.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/with-server-pagination.ts).

## Connecting a feature to a store's own signals

A feature that takes a signal as a parameter is reused with any store that has one. `withFeature` hands the store to a
function that returns the feature:

```ts
function withOrderLabel(orderId: Signal<number>) {
  return signalStoreFeature(withComputed(() => ({ label: computed(() => `Order #${orderId()}`) })));
}

export const OrderHeaderStore = signalStore(
  withState({ orderId: 0 }),
  withFeature(({ orderId }) => withOrderLabel(orderId)),
);
```

This replaces the toolkit's deprecated `withFeatureFactory`. See [order-header.store.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/order-header.store.ts).

## State that follows other state

`withLinkedState` adds writable state that is computed from other signals and resets itself when its source changes. Use it
instead of an `effect` that sets state:

```ts
withLinkedState(({ options }) => ({
  selectedOption: linkedSignal<Option[], Option | undefined>({
    source: options,
    computation: (next, previous) => next.find(o => o.id === previous?.value?.id) ?? next[0],
  }),
})),
```

The selection survives a refetch if the option still exists, and falls back to the first one if not. The file is
[options.store.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/options.store.ts).

For a function that reacts to a signal and doesn't need operators, `signalMethod` is lighter than `rxMethod`.

## When stores must talk to each other

Stores should not inject each other. When two stores really need to coordinate (a cart that changes when an order is
placed), use the events plugin from `@ngrx/signals/events`. One side dispatches a named event, the other reacts to it, and
neither knows the other exists.

```ts
export const cartEvents = eventGroup({
  source: 'Cart',
  events: {
    added: type<{ sku: string; qty: number }>(),
    cleared: type<void>(),
  },
});

export const CartStore = signalStore(
  { providedIn: 'root' },
  withState({ lines: {} as Record<string, number> }),
  withReducer(
    on(cartEvents.added, ({ payload }, state) => ({
      lines: { ...state.lines, [payload.sku]: (state.lines[payload.sku] ?? 0) + payload.qty },
    })),
    on(cartEvents.cleared, () => ({ lines: {} })),
  ),
);
```

A component dispatches with `injectDispatch(cartEvents).added({ sku, qty })`. See [cart-events.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/cart-events.ts)
and [cart.store.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/cart.store.ts). This is the replacement for the toolkit's `withRedux`, and it is
the answer to "billing needs something from orders" in [01-architecture.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/01-architecture.md). Use it sparingly: most
state is one page's state, and a page's store is enough.

## Rules

<!-- rules -->
- Write a custom `signalStoreFeature` only after the same block has been copied between stores three times.
- Use one `status` field (`idle | loading | success | error`) instead of separate `loading`, `error` and `loaded` flags in `rxMethod` stores.
- Do not use `withRequestStatus` with resources or mutations; they already track their own status.
- Declare what a feature needs from the store with `type<>()` as its first argument so the compiler checks order.
- Connect a reusable feature to a store's own signals with `withFeature`, not `withFeatureFactory`.
- Use `withLinkedState` or `linkedSignal` for state that follows other state instead of an `effect` that sets signals.
- Use `signalMethod` for reactions that need no operators, and `rxMethod` when they do.
- Never inject one store into another; coordinate stores with `@ngrx/signals/events` event groups.
<!-- /rules -->

---

# Forms, routing, translations and right-to-left

The parts of an app that every screen touches: how a form validates, how a route loads, how text is translated, and how the
layout flips for Arabic.

## Forms

**Reactive Forms are the default.** Validators and input directives (digits only, trimmed text, IBAN-shaped, and so on)
live in a shared `validators` and `directives` library and are written against Reactive Forms, so every form gets them for
free.

- A form control is typed: `new FormControl('', { nonNullable: true })`, never an untyped `FormControl(null)`.
- Validators are functions in the shared library, named for what they check. Error messages are translation keys keyed by the
  validator's error name, so the template maps `errors` to `t('errors.' + key)` once, in a shared error component.
- A form with unsaved changes extends a small `FormDeactivate` base and is protected by a `canDeactivate` guard, so leaving
  the page asks first.
- Sanitise on the way in, not only on the server: trim text and reject markup that has no business in the field. See the
  reason check in [cancel-order-dialog.component.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/testing/examples/cancel-order-dialog.component.ts).
- A submit button is disabled while the request is pending and a second click is ignored in code as well, because disabled
  is a visual state and not a guarantee.

Angular 22 ships Signal Forms as public API, with parts still marked experimental. They are the likely future of forms. This
guide stays on Reactive Forms for now because the shared validators and directives are built on them, and mixing two form
systems in one app costs more than either saves. A small new form in a codebase with no such investment may reasonably try
Signal Forms.

## Routing

- **Lazy by default.** Every feature is a `loadComponent` or `loadChildren`. Only the shell is in the main bundle.
- **One routes file per feature**, named `<feature>.routes.ts`, exporting a `Routes` array. The app's route table only points
  at features, it doesn't list their children.
- **Bind route data to inputs** with `withComponentInputBinding()`, so a page declares `orderId = input<string>()` instead of
  injecting `ActivatedRoute`.
- **Page titles are translation keys** in the route's `title`, resolved by a title strategy that translates them.
- **Guards are functional and built by factories**: `createRoleGuard('manager')`, `createPermissionGuard(Permission.Refunds)`.
  A factory keeps the rule in the route table where reviewers read it.
- **Unauthenticated and authenticated pages sit under different shells**, each with its own layout.

```ts
export const routes: Routes = [
  {
    path: 'orders',
    title: 'titles.orders',
    canActivate: [authGuard, createRoleGuard('manager')],
    loadChildren: () => import('@shop/orders/feature/orders').then(m => m.ORDERS_ROUTES),
  },
];
```

Provide `withComponentInputBinding()` and a preloading strategy in `app.config.ts`. `PreloadAllModules` is a fine start for
an app of this size; switch to a custom strategy when the bundle list grows.

## Translations

The app uses Transloco with one file per language, `public/i18n/en.json` and `public/i18n/ar.json`.

- **Every key exists in every language file.** A missing Arabic key is a bug caught in review, and the test setup logs it
  (see `provideTestTransloco` in [09-testing.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/09-testing.md)).
- Keys are camelCase and nested by feature: `orders.cancel.reasonRequired`.
- A template uses the structural directive once at the top, with a prefix: `*transloco="let t; prefix: 'orders.cancel'"`.
- Stores, interceptors and services carry **keys**, never translated strings. The template translates.
- A read that depends on language (an `Accept-Language` header) reads the language signal inside its request, so a language
  change refetches. See [OrderDetailsComponent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/testing/examples/order-details.component.ts).
- Format dates and numbers through one helper that takes the language as a parameter, so Arabic digits and calendars are
  decided in one place, and the helper stays a pure function.

## Right-to-left

Arabic is not a translation file, it is a layout. The language store exposes a `dir` computed, and the root element binds it:

```ts
// layout.store.ts
withComputed(({ language }) => ({
  isRtl: computed(() => language() === 'ar'),
  dir: computed(() => (language() === 'ar' ? 'rtl' : 'ltr')),
})),
```

Then write styles so they need no per-language code:

- **Use logical properties**, never left and right. With utility classes that is `ms-4` and `pe-2` instead of `ml-4` and
  `pr-2`, `text-start` instead of `text-left`, `start-0` instead of `left-0`.
- **Mirror directional icons**: arrows, chevrons, "back" and "next". Icons that carry no direction (a magnifier, a bin) stay.
- **Don't mirror** numerals, logos, charts' time axes, phone numbers or code.
- **Use a font with Arabic glyphs** as the primary font, not as a fallback, so the two scripts have matching weight and height.
- **Test it.** Switch the language in a spec (`layout.fake.language.set('ar')`) and assert on what changes, and look at every
  new screen in Arabic once before merging.

## Rules

<!-- rules -->
- Use Reactive Forms as the default; build validators and input directives in a shared library and reuse them.
- Type every form control; use `nonNullable` controls.
- Make validator error messages translation keys keyed by the error name.
- Protect forms with unsaved changes with a `canDeactivate` guard.
- Trim and reject unwanted markup in form input in code, and ignore a second submit while a request is pending.
- Lazy-load every feature with `loadComponent` or `loadChildren`; keep one `<feature>.routes.ts` per feature.
- Use `withComponentInputBinding()` and read route values through `input()`, not `ActivatedRoute`.
- Put translation keys in route `title`; build guards with factory functions such as `createRoleGuard`.
- Provide an entry for every key in every language file; keep keys camelCase and nested by feature.
- Carry translation keys in stores, interceptors and services; translate only in templates.
- Read the language signal inside a request that depends on language so it refetches on change.
- Expose a `dir` computed from the language store and bind it on the root element.
- Use logical properties (`ms-*`, `pe-*`, `text-start`, `start-*`), never physical left and right.
- Mirror directional icons in right-to-left; do not mirror numerals, logos or code.
<!-- /rules -->

---

# Accessibility

Accessibility is part of "done". It is cheap to build in from the first commit and expensive to retrofit, and the people it
protects are not a small group: anyone on a phone in sunlight, anyone using a keyboard, anyone whose first language is read
right to left.

## Measure contrast, don't judge it

Eyes lie, especially on your own monitor. Measure.

| Text | Minimum ratio |
| --- | --- |
| Small text (under 18px, or under 14px bold) | **7:1** |
| Any other text | 4.5:1 |
| Large text, icons, input borders, focus rings | 3:1 |

7:1 for small text is stricter than the WCAG AA minimum of 4.5:1. It is the AAA level, and it is what keeps small labels
readable on a phone outdoors. [templates/a11y/contrast.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/a11y/contrast.ts) is a 15-line function that returns the
ratio between two hex colours, and its spec pins known values.

A brand colour is usually the problem. A saturated blue such as `#0059ff` on a near-black `#101820` measures 3.3:1. That is
fine for a large heading or a filled button, and unreadable as a 12px label. So:

- **Brand colours are for fills, borders and large text.** Small text uses a neutral token with a measured ratio.
- **Define text colours as design tokens** and check the token pairs once, rather than checking every screen.
- **Check dark mode separately.** A pair that passes on white can fail on dark.

## Meaning never rides on colour alone

A red border is not an error message. Pair every colour signal with text, an icon or a pattern:

- An invalid field shows an icon and a message, and the control has `aria-invalid="true"`.
- A status is a word ("Paid", "Cancelled") as well as a colour, and a chart series has a label or a pattern as well as a hue.
- A required field says "required" in text, not only with a coloured asterisk.

## Keyboard and focus

- Every interactive element is reachable with Tab, in reading order, and operable with Enter or Space. Use a real `<button>`
  or `<a>`, not a clickable `<div>`.
- Focus is always visible. Don't remove the outline; restyle it with a colour that meets 3:1 against its surroundings.
- A dialog moves focus in when it opens, traps it while open and returns it to the trigger on close.
- After a route change, move focus to the page heading so a screen reader announces where it landed.
- Don't use positive `tabindex`.

## Names, roles and announcements

- Every control has an accessible name: a `<label for>`, or `aria-label` for an icon button.
- Use native elements before ARIA. `aria-*` repairs a missing semantic; it doesn't replace one.
- Errors and status changes that appear without a page load use `role="alert"` or `aria-live="polite"`.
- A list that is loading carries `aria-busy`, as in [order-list.component.html](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/signal-store/order-list.component.html).
- Images have `alt`; decorative ones have `alt=""`.

## Size and motion

- Body text is at least 16px, and nothing meaningful is under 12px. Check at phone scale, not on a desktop monitor.
- Touch targets are at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: turn off parallax, large slides and autoplay for those users.
- Don't rely on hover for anything a touch user needs.

## Let the tools catch the easy ones

Enable the `templateAccessibility` config from `angular-eslint` in the shared ESLint config and leave it on. The common
temptation is to switch a rule off to ship a form; fix the markup instead. Automated checks catch only part of the problems,
so also tab through every new screen once with the mouse unplugged.

## Rules

<!-- rules -->
- Measure contrast with a function or tool; require 7:1 for small text, 4.5:1 for other text, and 3:1 for large text, icons, borders and focus rings.
- Use brand colours only for fills, borders and large text; give small text a neutral token with a measured ratio.
- Check light and dark themes separately.
- Never let colour alone carry meaning; pair it with text, an icon or a pattern.
- Mark invalid controls with `aria-invalid` and show the error as text.
- Use native `<button>` and `<a>` for interactive elements; never a clickable `<div>`.
- Keep focus visible with at least 3:1 contrast; never remove the outline without replacing it.
- Move focus into a dialog on open, trap it while open, and return it on close; move focus to the heading after a route change.
- Give every control an accessible name; prefer native elements over ARIA.
- Announce dynamic errors and status changes with `role="alert"` or `aria-live`.
- Keep body text at 16px or more, touch targets at 44px or more, and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Enable the Angular ESLint template accessibility rules and do not switch them off to ship.
<!-- /rules -->

---

# Testing

A unit test answers one question: **given these inputs and these collaborators, does this file do the right thing?** This
chapter is the way I write specs, and [templates/testing/](https://github.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/blob/main/templates/testing/) is the toolkit that makes it quick. All of it
runs on Jest 30 with `jest-preset-angular`, zoneless. With Vitest, replace `jest.fn` and `jest.spyOn` with `vi.fn` and
`vi.spyOn`; nothing else changes.

## The idea

- The file under test is **real**. Everything it `inject()`s is a **fake** you control.
- Every test starts from a **fresh world**: new fakes, a new component, nothing left over from the last test.
- A test asserts on what the file **does**: what it renders, what its public signals hold, what it asked its collaborators
  to do. Never on private fields.

And four things that are not used in specs:

| Don't | Because | Do instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TestBed.configureTestingModule` in a spec | Boilerplate that hides what the test is about | `render`, `renderPage`, `injectService` |
| `{ provide: Service, useValue: {...} }` | Untyped, shared between tests, drifts from the real API | `fakeService(Service, () => ({...}))` |
| `HttpTestingController` | Verbose, and doesn't work with `httpResource` as naturally | `fakeHttp({ url: body })` |
| `as jest.Mock` casts | Hide wrong types | `fakeService` is typed, so `fake.method` is already a mock |

The only `useValue` allowed is for an injection token such as `DOCUMENT` or `PLATFORM_ID`.

## The toolkit

Copy [templates/testing/](https://github.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/blob/main/templates/testing/) to `src/app/core/test/`, map `@/core/test` in `tsconfig` and Jest
([jest.config.example.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/testing/jest.config.example.js) shows how), and import from that one place.

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Render a component | `render(Component, providers, options?)` |
| Render a routed page (adds translations) | `renderPage(Component, providers, options?)` |
| Get a service or a store | `injectService(Service, [Service, ...fakes])` |
| Run an `inject()` function (guard, resolver) | `runInContext(() => guard(route, state), fakes)` |
| Fake any service | `fakeService(Service, () => ({ method: jest.fn() }))` |
| Fake HTTP, including `httpResource` | `fakeHttp({ '/api/x': body, '/api/y': httpError(500) })` |
| Router and route | `fakeRouter()`, `fakeRoute({ params, queryParams, data })` |
| Storage | `fakeStorage(StorageService, { language: 'en' })` |
| Force a resource state | `setResource(resource, { value } / { status } / { error })` |
| Run pending effects | `flushEffects()` |
| Wait for async work and render | `await view.whenStable()` |

### What a fake gives you

```ts
const files = fakeService(FileDownloadService, () => ({ save: jest.fn() }));

files.fake.save; // the live fake the component received, typed, a jest.Mock here
expect(files.fake.save).toHaveBeenCalledWith('order-77.json', expect.any(String));
```

- `x.fake` is the instance the code under test is using **in this test**.
- The **factory form** `() => ({ ... })` builds a new fake per test, so no `jest.clearAllMocks()` is ever needed.
- Helpers with controls expose them on `x._`: `http._.reply(url, body)`, `http._.calls(url)`, `route._.setQueryParams({...})`.
- Types come from the real service. If the real member is a signal, the fake is a `signal(...)`; if it is an observable, use
  `of(...)` or a `Subject`. A wrong shape fails to compile, which is how stubs faking APIs that no longer exist get found.

### What a view gives you

| Read the DOM | Act like a user | Drive the component |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `view.$('css' or Component)`, `view.$All(...)` | `.click()`, `.input('x')`, `.type('x')` | `view.host`, the instance |
| `view.$testId('LOGIN_BTN')` | `.keydown('Enter')`, `.paste('x')` | `view.setInput('name', value)`, typed |
| `view.getByText('Cancel')` | `.focus()`, `.mouseEnter()` | `view.detectChanges()` |
| `.textContent`, `.attr()`, `.hasClass()` | | `view.inject(Service)` |

Typed `setInput` uses Angular's private `ɵINPUT_SIGNAL_BRAND_WRITE_TYPE`. That is the one private API in the toolkit; if a
future Angular renames it, one type in `testing-utils.ts` is the only line to change.

## The recipe

1. Read the file, and its template, and classify it.
2. List every injection.
3. Pick a fake for each one.
4. List the behaviours and branches, as test names, before writing code.
5. Decide the describes.
6. Write the spec.
7. Run with coverage and close the gaps.

### 1. Classify

| Kind | Build it with |
| --- | --- |
| Service, store, guard class | `injectService(Service, [Service, ...fakes])` |
| Component with no translations | `render(Component, fakes)` |
| Page or component using Transloco | `renderPage(Component, fakes)` |
| Directive or pipe | `render(TestHost, fakes)` with a tiny host component |
| Pure function | Call it directly. No Angular needed |

### 2. List every injection

Collect them from five places: `inject()` fields, constructor parameters, `inject*` helper functions (open them to see what
they inject), `httpResource` and `resource` calls (`httpResource` uses `HttpClient`), and the component's own `providers`
plus its child components, since rendering builds those too.

**An injection you don't use still has to be satisfied.** A component that injects a toaster but never calls it still makes
Angular build the real one, and the real one may need a library service you didn't expect. The first run fails with
`NG0201: No provider found`. Fake it with an empty object.

### 3. Pick a fake

Go top to bottom and stop at the first rule that fits:

| The injection is | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| `HttpClient`, including `httpResource` | `fakeHttp({ url: body })` |
| `Router` or `ActivatedRoute` | `fakeRouter()` or `fakeRoute({ params })` |
| Translations | Real, through `renderPage` |
| A root store that is plain state with no dependencies | Keep it **real** and seed it through its own methods |
| Anything else | `fakeService(X, () => ({ onlyWhatIsUsed: jest.fn() }))` |
| An injection token | `{ provide: TOKEN, useValue }` |

Two rules for `fakeService`: **fake only what the code uses** (`{ save: jest.fn() }` is enough when only `save()` is called),
and **match the real types** so the fake can't drift.

When a service is also declared in the component's own `providers`, a fake in the shared list is ignored, because the
component's provider wins. Use the `providers` option, which overrides everywhere:

```ts
view = await renderPage(Component, providers, { providers: [fakeService(Toaster, {})] });
```

### 4. List behaviours before writing code

Walk the file and note every place it can go two ways: `if`, `?:`, `&&`, `??`, `?.`, `@if`, `@for` with `@empty`, `@switch`,
`next` and `error` callbacks, every public method and every computed. Write one line per behaviour:

- renders the title and no error before the user does anything
- confirming with an empty, blank or HTML reason shows the error and sends nothing
- confirming with a valid reason sends the trimmed text and the id from the dialog
- while sending, it shows loading, disables Back and ignores a second click
- the API says yes: the dialog closes with `true`
- the API says no: the dialog stays open

Each line is one `it(...)`, named as a sentence. Variants of one check use `it.each`.

### 5. Decide the describes

This is the step people get wrong most often.

> **A top-level `describe` is one world: one set of providers, fixed when the component is created.**
> **A nested `describe` groups tests that share an extra `beforeEach` action inside that world.**

For each condition ask: *can I change it from inside a test, through a fake?*

| Same describe: a test can change it | New top-level describe: it can't |
| --- | --- |
| A fake's signal: `language.fake.language.set('ar')` | Something read once in a constructor or field initialiser |
| A fake's return value: `x.fake.get.mockReturnValue(...)` | The route snapshot: `fakeRoute({ params })` |
| A later HTTP answer: `http._.reply(url, body)` then reload | Dialog data |
| User input: `.input()`, `.click()`, `setInput()` | The first HTTP answer, when you assert the first render |
| | A component-level provider |

For the second column, add a top-level describe that swaps only that one fake through `options.providers`:

```ts
describe('OrderDetailsComponent when the API fails', () => {
  it('shows the error instead of the order', async () => {
    const view = await renderPage(OrderDetailsComponent, providers, {
      providers: [fakeHttp({ [ORDER_URL]: httpError(500) })],
    });
    await view.whenStable();
    ...
```

Trying to swap a fake inside a test fails with "Cannot configure the test module when the test module has already been
instantiated". That error means you need another describe.

### 6. Write the spec

Every spec has the same shape. [order-details.component.spec.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/testing/examples/order-details.component.spec.ts)
is the complete version:

```ts
// 1. Fakes: one per injection, at module level, factory form.
const http = fakeHttp({ [ORDER_URL]: order });
const route = fakeRoute({ params: { orderId: '77' } });

// 2. The shared provider list.
const providers = [provideRouter([]), http, route, language, files];

// 3. One describe per world.
describe('OrderDetailsComponent', () => {
  let view: RenderResult<OrderDetailsComponent>;

  // 4. Build the world in beforeEach.
  beforeEach(async () => {
    view = await renderPage(OrderDetailsComponent, providers);
    await view.whenStable(); // let httpResource load and the template render
  });

  // 5. One behaviour per it, named as a sentence.
  it('loads the order named in the route', () => {
    expect(http._.calls(ORDER_URL)).toBe(1);
    expect(view.$testId('ORDER_TITLE').textContent).toBe('Order 77');
  });
});

// 6. Variant worlds swap one fake.
```

Habits that keep specs readable:

- **Arrange, act, assert**, with a blank line between.
- **Name helpers after what the user does**, so tests read like a story:
  `const confirmButton = () => view.getByText('Confirm')` and `const answer = (ok: boolean) => api.fake.cancel.mock.calls[0][1](https://github.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/blob/main/docs/ok)`.
- **Prefer the DOM and public signals** over private members. Use `component['x']` rather than `as any` only when there is no public way.
- **Make test data `satisfies` the real model**: `const order = { ... } satisfies Order;`, so a renamed field fails to compile.

### 7. Coverage

Run one spec with coverage for its source file, then read the uncovered lines. For each gap decide:

| The gap is | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| A real state you haven't tested | Add the test |
| Code that can never run (a `?.` after validation, an unused `computed`) | Simplify the code if behaviour stays the same, and list the edit in the pull request |
| Can't be simplified safely | `/* istanbul ignore next */` with a one-line reason |

## Cookbook

**HTTP.**

```ts
const http = fakeHttp({
  '/api/orders': { items: [] }, // a body; the longest matching key wins
  '/api/limits': httpError(500), // an error reply
});

http._.reply('/api/orders', { items: [a] }); // change the answer for later requests in this test
http._.calls('/api/orders'); // how many requests hit it
expect(http.fake.post).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/api/x', body);

const slow = fakeHttp({}, { pending: true }); // every request waits
slow._.flush('/api/orders', body); // answer it
slow._.fail('/api/orders', 403); // or fail it
```

An unknown URL fails with `fakeHttp: no route for GET /api/...`, so a missing route never passes silently.

**Resources.** Prefer the real thing: serve the data with `fakeHttp` and `await view.whenStable()`. To reload after changing
the answer: `http._.reply(...)`, `view.host.order.reload()`, `await view.whenStable()`. To force a state without HTTP, use
`setResource(view.host.list, { status: 'reloading' })` **before** the first `detectChanges` that reads the resource, because
a `computed` that already read it keeps its cached value.

**A callback passed to a service.** Capture it, then fire it when the test is ready, as the dialog spec does with `answer(true)`.

**Signals in fakes.** Put `signal(...)` in the factory and change it with `x.fake.sig.set(...)`, as `language` does in the page spec.

**Inputs and outputs.**

```ts
view = await render(Card, [], { inputs: { title: 'Hello' } }); // typed against the component
view.setInput('amount', '42'); // typed, accepts the input's transform type
const value = await firstOutputFrom(view.host.saved); // the next output emission
```

**Effects and timers.** `flushEffects()` runs pending effects. `jest.useFakeTimers()` with `advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ms)`
covers `setTimeout` and debounce. A store spec's version of `whenStable` is a small `settle()` that flushes effects, lets the
resource finish and flushes again, as in [order-list.store.spec.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/testing/examples/order-list.store.spec.ts).

**A store.** `injectService(Store, [Store, http])`, call its methods, assert on its signals. See the same file.

## Pitfalls

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `NG0201: No provider found for X` | Something in the tree injects X. Fake it, even if your file never calls it |
| A fake in `providers` is ignored | The component declares that service in its own `providers`. Use `{ providers: [fake] }` in the options |
| "Cannot configure the test module ... already instantiated" | You swapped a fake inside a test. Make a new top-level describe |
| The DOM still shows the loading state | `httpResource` hasn't settled. `await view.whenStable()` |
| `setResource` has no effect | It ran after a `computed` cached the real value. Call it before the first `detectChanges` |
| A boolean input is always on | You passed `signal(false)` instead of `false`. Typed `setInput` catches it |
| Tests pass alone and fail together | A shared mutable object at module level. Use the factory form of `fakeService` |
| A debounced store never updates | Fake timers are on but effects weren't flushed. Call `flushEffects()`, then advance the timers |

## Review checklist

- Every `inject()` in the file and in its children is satisfied by a fake, or kept real on purpose.
- No `TestBed`, no `useValue` for services, no `as jest.Mock`, no `HttpTestingController`.
- Fakes are module-level and use the factory form. The provider list is shared.
- One top-level describe per world; variants swap one fake through `options.providers`.
- Test names are sentences about behaviour, and each `it` checks one behaviour.
- Every branch in the `.ts` and the template has a test, or a listed code simplification.
- The new spec is at full coverage for its file, and the whole suite is green.

## Rules

<!-- rules -->
- Test the real file with fakes for everything it injects; start every test from a fresh world.
- Assert on behaviour (DOM, public signals, calls on fakes), never on private fields.
- Never use `TestBed.configureTestingModule` directly, `{ provide, useValue }` for services, `HttpTestingController` or `as jest.Mock` in specs.
- Import every test utility from `@/core/test`.
- Fake services with `fakeService(X, () => ({ ... }))` in the factory form, at module level, one per `inject()`.
- Fake only what the code uses, and match the real types so the fake cannot drift.
- Fake HTTP, including `httpResource`, with `fakeHttp`; let unknown URLs fail loudly.
- Satisfy every injection in the tree, including ones the code never calls.
- Keep a root store real when it is plain state with no dependencies, and seed it through its own methods.
- Write one top-level `describe` per world; use a new top-level describe with `options.providers` for anything a test cannot change through a fake.
- Name tests as sentences, check one behaviour per `it`, and use `it.each` for variants of one check.
- List the behaviours and branches before writing the spec.
- Make test data `satisfies` the real model.
- Give every store, service, guard and component a spec beside it.
- Wait with `await view.whenStable()`; for stores flush effects and then settle the resource.
<!-- /rules -->

---

# Tooling

The tools are chosen so that the rules in this guide are enforced by the machine. Every config below is in
[templates/config/](https://github.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/blob/main/templates/config/) and is the one in use, not a suggestion.

## The stack

| Area | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Framework | Angular 22 (standalone, zoneless, signals) |
| Language | TypeScript 6.0, strict |
| State | NgRx Signals 22, `@ngrx-toolkit/core` 22 |
| Workspace | Nx, pnpm |
| Tests | Jest 30 with `jest-preset-angular` |
| Lint and format | ESLint (flat config) with `angular-eslint`, Prettier |
| Commits | Conventional Commits with an emoji, Husky, lint-staged, commitlint |

The versions are the ones Angular supports. Angular 22 accepts TypeScript `>=6.0 <6.1`, so the TypeScript range moves with
the Angular major, never ahead of it. Check [angular.dev/reference/versions](https://angular.dev/reference/versions) before
you bump either.

## pnpm and Nx

- **Always pnpm.** One package manager, one lockfile. Run Nx through it: `pnpm nx test orders-data-access`.
- **Nx owns the targets.** In an Nx workspace there is no `angular.json`; each project's `project.json` defines build, test
  and lint. Where Angular's docs say `ng build`, run `pnpm nx build <project>`, and use the Nx generators instead of
  `ng generate`.
- `pnpm nx affected -t lint,test` runs only what the current change touches. It is the command CI and a pre-push hook use.
- Name scripts `domain:action` (`start:dev`, `build:ci`, `test:ci`) and keep them in the root `package.json`.

## TypeScript

[tsconfig.strict.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/config/tsconfig.strict.json) turns on `strict`, `noImplicitOverride`,
`noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature`, `noImplicitReturns` and the Angular compiler's `strictTemplates`. Strict templates
catch a binding to a renamed signal at build time, which is half the reason to rename things confidently. Do not turn strict
flags off to make a build pass; fix the type.

## ESLint

A flat config at the root, `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` for the architecture rules
([eslint.boundaries.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/config/eslint.boundaries.js)), and `angular-eslint` for components and templates. The rules
that matter most:

- `prefer-standalone` and the signal-input rules, as errors.
- The template accessibility config, on and left on. See [08-accessibility.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/08-accessibility.md).
- `no-restricted-imports` for sibling entry points, as described in [01-architecture.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/docs/01-architecture.md).
- No `any`. Where an `any` is truly needed, write `// eslint-disable-next-line` with the reason beside it.

## Prettier

[.prettierrc.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/config/.prettierrc.json) is short and has no options worth arguing over:

- 120 columns, 2 spaces, single quotes, `trailingComma: all`, `arrowParens: avoid`.
- `singleAttributePerLine` and `bracketSameLine`, so a template diff shows one attribute per changed line.
- `@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports` with the order `@angular/*`, then `rxjs`, then third-party, then relative.
- `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` sorts utility classes, and `*.html` uses the `angular` parser.

Pair it with [.editorconfig](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomavic/angular-philosophies/main/templates/config/.editorconfig). Formatting is never a review comment: the hook formats, so a
reviewer reads logic.

## Commits and hooks

- **Conventional Commits with an emoji:** `fix(orders-data-access): 🐛 keep the page when a reload fails`. The scope is the project
